| Enigma | covered | `enigma:encrypt` | Enigma I, M3 and M4 with the historical rotors, reflectors and plugboard; one reciprocal word (alias decrypt). |
| Bombe | redesigned | `bombe:search` | One Forge-native word covers both Bombe operations: give three rotors for a single rotor order. It searches all 17,576 start positions with a crib at an offset, using the menu, the diagonal board and the test register, and lists the stops with the steckers deduced and a decryption preview made with enigma:encrypt. Enigma I and M3 only (no M4); stops are window letters at the start of the message. |
| Multiple Bombe | redesigned | `bombe:search` | The same word: give more than three rotors (up to five, 60 orders) and every order of three of them is searched, left rotor first; the output names the rotor order of each stop. Capped by rotor orders times menu edges so that a run finishes inside a bake. |
| Typex | redesigned | `typex:encrypt` | Real Typex rotor wirings were never published, so there is no built-in rotor set: the five rotor wirings, reflector, notches and reversed rotors are parameters (validated permutations of A-Z), with clearly labelled non-historical example defaults. The conventions (rotors written left to right with the signal entering at the right, notch letters tested after the step, reversed rotors as neg o inverse o neg, the entry plugboard as a 26-letter wiring entering c as -P(c), Enigma-style stepping with the double step) follow CyberChef's for compatibility; the real Typex conventions are unpublished. |
| Lorenz | redesigned | `lorenz:encrypt`, `lorenz:decrypt` | Two words with one set of parameters (model SZ40, SZ42a or SZ42b, the P5 attachment, KH, ZMUG, BREAM or custom wheel patterns, twelve start positions, text or ITA2 in and out); decrypt exists because the P5 limitation makes the key depend on the plain text. |
| Colossus | redesigned | `colossus:count` | A counting run over the start positions of two chi wheels with a Boolean condition on delta Z and delta chi (the 1+2 break-in by default), a set total and a table of the best settings; it does not model the plug panels and the tape reader of the machine, and it does not search three wheels at once. |
| SIGABA | covered | `sigaba:crypt` | One word with a mode parameter (encrypt or decrypt), the rotor choice, orientation (R suffix) and start positions of the three banks, and optional rotor wirings; the default wirings are Forge's own, not the historical ones. The index rotor offset (+d for digit d) follows CyberChef's convention for compatibility; the sources do not fix it. |

## Flow control (10)

| CyberChef | Status | Forge | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Magic | not yet |  |  |
| Fork | redesigned | `step:fork` | A structural fork step (RECIPES section 3.2) holds its child steps; split and join are part of the step. |
| Subsection | redesigned | `step:subsection` | A structural step that runs its children on each regex match and leaves the rest of the data alone. |
| Merge | redesigned | `step:fork` | No separate step: a fork step joins its pieces when its children end. |
| Register | not yet |  |  |
| Label | redesigned | `step:repeat` | Loops are structural repeat steps (a count or until stable), not labels. |
| Jump | redesigned | `step:repeat` | Loops are structural repeat steps (a count or until stable), not jumps. |
| Conditional Jump | redesigned | `step:if` | Branching is a tree: an if step holds then and else steps, so there are no labels or jumps. |
| Return | not yet |  |  |
| Comment | redesigned | `step:comment` | A structural comment step with no effect on the data. |
